title: Event envelope
description: Every durable event carries these fields. They are what a consumer can rely on without knowing the event type, which is what makes generic handling, deduplication and audit possible. Restricted content never appears here or in a payload, because events reach integrations and analytics where the retention and access rules belong to somebody else. See ADR-0004.

event_id.description: UUIDv7. Consumers deduplicate on this, which is what makes at-least-once delivery safe, so it is stable across every redelivery of the same fact.

event_type.description: The contract a consumer subscribes against, including its version. evaluation.completed.v1 and evaluation.completed.v2 are different events that may be emitted side by side during a migration.

schema_version.description: How the payload has evolved within this contract. It bumps for additive change; a consumer tolerates a higher value rather than refusing it, because refusing one is how an additive change becomes a breaking one.

tenant_id.description: The tenant the fact belongs to. Absent for a fact that predates tenant selection, such as a registration, which is why it is not required.

occurred_at.description: When the fact happened, not when it was delivered. Delivery may be much later and may be out of order, so ordering by receipt is a mistake a consumer must not be led into.

producer.description: The bounded context that owns the authoritative state. Only it emits this event.

actor.description: Who or what caused the fact. Present on every event because an audit trail that cannot name an actor answers no question worth asking.

purpose.description: Which authority the fact arose under. Practice and screening are separated everywhere, and a consumer that mixes them has broken the separation on our behalf.

correlation_id.description: Ties every event arising from one originating request together.

causation_id.description: The event_id of the event that caused this one, so a chain can be walked backwards without guessing from timestamps.

payload.description: The event-type-specific body, validated against that type's schema at publication.

type.description: system is for a fact nobody triggered, such as an expiry. Distinguished from service so that 'nobody did this' is not recorded as 'a worker did this'.

id.description: The user identifier, or the service name. Never an email address, which is restricted content.
